info.description: Public API for the MyGameDNA skill-based games classification platform. Exposes game identities, Challenge and Reward classification profiles, search, rankings, and catalogue data.
info.title: MyGameDNA API

get.description: Returns the API product name and version.

Return a deterministic paginated list of publicly-listed base Games. Supports name search, source filter, classification filter, dominant skill-category filter, primary sorting (name, recently added, or a Challenge/Reward Micro/Mystiko/Macro score), an optional cover-last outer partition, and pagination.  Reads persisted state only — never contacts Steam and never recalculates classification.
Return up to 10 randomly selected publicly-listed Steam base Games that have a Library Capsule, for the homepage carousel.  Reads persisted state only — never contacts Steam.
get.summary: Get random homepage Steam carousel games

get.description: Return the complete compact search index of publicly-listed base Games (slug, name, effective Capsule, and effective general image) for client-side autocomplete.  Deterministic (name ASC, id ASC); reads persisted state only — never contacts Steam, never probes images, and never recalculates classification.

post.description: Import (or re-import) one Steam App ID into canonical storage. Returns CREATED, UPDATED, UNCHANGED, or UNAVAILABLE with the canonical Game summary when a Game exists.
Refresh one canonical Steam Game from Steam metadata.  The Game is identified by its internal ID; the persisted Steam identity is the only App ID used.  Returns UPDATED, UNCHANGED, or UNAVAILABLE.

get.description: Return the normalized public identity and persisted metadata for one publicly-listed base Game, together with its currently persisted Final Classification (if any).  Reads persisted state only — never contacts Steam and never recalculates classification.

Return a deterministic paginated ranking of publicly-listed base Games. Supports the Unified/Challenge/Reward profile, a Micro/Macro/Mystiko dimension, ascending/descending direction, an optional dominant-category filter, and pagination.  Unified scores are (Challenge + Reward) / 2 and may end in .5.  Reads persisted state only — never contacts Steam and never recalculates classification.
